stances.claim: Javellana validated the 1973 ratification by raising of hands and thereby effectively validated Marcos's martial law and PD-issuance powers -- a 6-4 outcome whose break from paper-ballot plebiscitary tradition is the foundational departure CJ flags as 'notorious.'

Republic v. Sandiganbayan (July 15, 2003) forfeited $657M+ in Swiss deposits -- Marcos couple's total legal income being only $304K -- and the surplus-deemed-ill-gotten doctrine was followed by Yuchengco (2006) and Marcos v. Republic (2012); the PCGG claims P200B+ recovered in total.

Ocampo v. Enriquez's allowance of the LNMB interment of Marcos -- 'with ceremonies befitting a national hero' -- was a 'strange turnaround' from the forfeiture jurisprudence, and the Court's dictum that the matter is 'better left for history--not this Court--to adjudge' is one CJ disagrees with: 'This issue will not rest.'

Lambino correctly ruled that the parliamentary-system people's initiative was a 'grand deception' and 'gigantic fraud,' scuttling GMA's possible prime-ministership path -- but it reversed Santiago v. Comelec (1997), which had held the implementing law 'insufficient,' a reversal whose practical consequence was foreclosing FVR's re-election, 'arguably our best president since the 1987 Charter took effect.'

Bagong Bayani and Veterans Federation properly understood the Filipino-style party-list system as reserved for the marginalized and not mandatorily filling 20% of the House -- Atong Paglaum (2013) and Banat (2009) reversed both, opening party-list to dynasties, term-limit-circumventors, the rich, and the powerful at the expense of the marginalized.

Republic v. Sereno's 8-6 QW ouster of the CJ for unfiled SALNs as a UP professor was a 'legal abomination' (Leonen) -- and the unanimous Court refusal to release Leonen's own SALNs (which could have led to QW against him) hints at the present Court's sympathetic re-evaluation; the question is whether the Court will reverse and reinstate Sereno (or at least grant retirement benefits, as it did for Corona).
stances.confidence: asserted with conjectural marker ('the betting now')

notable_anecdotes: Javellana's raising-of-hands ratification -- a singular departure from the paper-ballot plebiscitary norm, used by CJ as the 'notorious' founding moment of the column's catalogue.

The arithmetic of the Swiss deposits forfeiture -- $657M+ versus Marcos couple's total legal income of only $304K -- the cleanest example of the surplus-deemed-ill-gotten doctrine, paired with the cumulative P200B+ PCGG recovery claim.

Ocampo v. Enriquez's 'strange turnaround' -- the same Court that forfeited the ill-gotten wealth allowing 'ceremonies befitting a national hero' at the LNMB; CJ's gentle 'With due respect, I disagree' is the strongest dissent he allows himself in a survey column.
Lambino's 'grand deception' and 'gigantic fraud' language -- the rare verbatim deployment of judicial denunciations because the underlying initiative was 'grand' enough to warrant it.

Santiago v. Comelec foregone-FVR-reelection counterfactual -- CJ's quietly bold 'arguably our best president since the 1987 Charter took effect' aside, the rare CJ on-the-record best-president opinion.

Party-list degradation enumeration -- dynasties, term-circumvention, the rich, the powerful -- laid out as a fourfold corruption with the 'richest House member is a party-list rep' as the headline indictment.
The Leonen-SALN/Sereno-QW symmetry diagnosis -- the Court unanimously refusing to release Leonen's SALNs that could have led to QW against him, used as the silent retrospective on the Sereno ouster.
Sereno-Corona retirement-benefit asymmetry: Sereno served 6 years (longer than Corona's 2) but Corona has been granted retirement benefits while Sereno has not.

one_paragraph_summary: Following his previous Sunday's catalog of five US cases, Panganiban inventories five Philippine SC decisions that game-changed our constitutional, political, and social landscape -- for better or for worse. First, the 'notorious' Javellana v. Executive Secretary (March 31, 1973, 6-4) upheld the ratification of the 1973 Constitution by raising of hands -- a departure from the paper-ballot plebiscitary tradition designed to protect voters from 'guns, goons and gold' -- and effectively validated Marcos's martial law and PD-issuance powers. Second, Republic v. Sandiganbayan (July 15, 2003, 14-0-1) forfeited $657M+ in Swiss deposits as Marcos ill-gotten wealth on the doctrine that whatever exceeded the Marcos couple's $304K legal income was ill-gotten; followed by Yuchengco (Jan 20, 2006 and Aug 6, 2006), Marcos v. Republic (April 25, 2012), and a cumulative P200B+ PCGG recovery. Yet in Ocampo v. Enriquez (Nov 8, 2016, 9-5-1), the Court allowed the LNMB interment of Marcos 'with ceremonies befitting a national hero' -- a 'strange turnaround' -- and concluded that 'there are certain things that are better left for history--not this Court--to adjudge.' With due respect, CJ disagrees: 'This issue will not rest; the Marcos saga is not over' given the political ascent of the Marcos scions. Third, Lambino v. Comelec (Oct 25, 2006, 8-7) correctly ruled the parliamentary-system people's initiative a 'grand deception' and 'gigantic fraud,' scuttling GMA's possible prime-ministership path -- but it reversed Santiago v. Comelec (March 19, 1997), which had held the implementing law 'insufficient,' and so foreclosed FVR's re-election ('arguably our best president since the 1987 Charter took effect'). Fourth, Bagong Bayani v. Comelec (June 26, 2001, 9-5-1) and Veterans Federation v. Comelec (Oct 6, 2000, 15-0) correctly reserved the Filipino-style party-list system for the marginalized and held the 20% House quota non-mandatory -- until Atong Paglaum (April 2, 2013) and Banat (April 21, 2009) reversed both, letting dynasties invade, veteran politicians circumvent the 3-term limit, the rich own the system, and the powerful misrepresent the lowly. Fifth, Republic v. Sereno (May 18, 2018, 8-6) ousted the chief justice via quo warranto for unfiled SALNs as a UP professor; Justice Leonen's dissent called it a 'legal abomination,' and the unanimous Court turning down a request for Leonen's own SALNs (which could have led to QW against him) hints at sympathetic re-evaluation. 'The betting now is whether the Court would reverse itself and reinstate Sereno, or, at least, grant her retirement benefits similar to what it did recently for CJ Renato C. Corona.'
